Turn 1 of 4 — read-back. Do not write any program JSON in this turn.

You are going to turn a recipe into a Rhylthyme program: parallel **tracks** of sequential **steps**, each with a duration and a start trigger, that one person follows against a live clock.

Plan this as a Rhylthyme recipe and deliver a live timeline: Breakfast for Six on One Griddle for 6 people
Resource limits: one griddle, one two-slice toaster, one coffee maker, one oven on its lowest setting, one cook.
Everything must be finished by 09:00.

Source text (read all of it):
<<<
Breakfast for Six on One Griddle

One electric griddle, a two-slice toaster, a burr grinder, a drip coffee maker and an oven turned to its lowest setting to hold things warm. One cook, six people, everyone eating at nine.

Prep
Whisk the dry pancake ingredients together, then beat in the buttermilk and eggs; 10 minutes. Let the batter stand for 20 minutes while the griddle does its first job. Crack a dozen eggs into a jug and season them; 5 minutes. Set the table and lay out six places; 10 minutes. Put six plates in the oven at its lowest setting and leave them there until you call everyone.

Griddle
Everything cooks on the one griddle, in order. Heat the griddle to 375°F; 8 minutes. Lay the bacon out and cook it for 14 minutes, turning once, then move it to the warm oven. Scrape the griddle and wipe off the fat; 3 minutes. Pancakes go on as soon as the griddle is clean and the batter has rested, in three passes: the first pass takes 6 minutes, the second another 6, and the third 6 more. Slide each pass into the oven as it comes off. Drop the griddle to 300°F and give it 4 minutes to settle, then scramble the eggs slowly for 7 minutes.

Toast
The toaster takes two slices at a time. Start the first batch of toast when the last pancake pass goes on; 3 minutes. Run a second batch straight after; 3 minutes. Butter all of it; 4 minutes.

Coffee
Start the grinder ten minutes after the bacon goes on so the pot is fresh. Grind the beans; 2 minutes. Brew a full pot; 9 minutes.

Serve
Call everyone when the eggs, the toast and the coffee are all ready, and carry the warm plates through; 5 minutes.
>>>

Read all of it before you answer. Then say back, in one paragraph and in your own words: what is being made, for how many (or at what scale), by when, and under what constraints — equipment that exists only once, how many people are working, anything that has to be held, rested or ready at a particular moment. If the text you were given looks truncated, or points at a section that is not here, say so instead of filling the gap.

End your reply with the same read-back as JSON in a single ```json fenced block:

```json
{
  "summary": "one paragraph: what is being made, for how many, by when, under what constraints",
  "servesOrScale": "8 people",
  "deadline": "2026-11-26T18:00:00",
  "constraints": ["one oven", "two burners", "two cooks"]
}
```

This is a one-cook, single-griddle breakfast for six people that must all be ready to serve at 09:00. It consists of bacon, buttermilk pancakes made in three passes, scrambled eggs, toasted bread, and coffee, with warm plates and cooked food held in an oven set to its lowest setting. The main constraints are that there is only one griddle, one two-slice toaster, one coffee maker, one burr grinder, and one cook, so many steps must be scheduled around the griddle; the pancake batter must rest for 20 minutes after mixing; the plates must be warmed in the oven; bacon and pancake passes must move into the warm oven after cooking; the toast batches must begin when the last pancake pass starts; and the coffee must begin ten minutes after the bacon goes on, with service waiting until the eggs, toast, and coffee are all finished.

```json
{
  "summary": "This is a one-cook, single-griddle breakfast for six people that must all be ready to serve at 09:00. It consists of bacon, buttermilk pancakes made in three passes, scrambled eggs, toasted bread, and coffee, with warm plates and cooked food held in an oven set to its lowest setting. The main constraints are that there is only one griddle, one two-slice toaster, one coffee maker, one burr grinder, and one cook, so many steps must be scheduled around the griddle; the pancake batter must rest for 20 minutes after mixing; the plates must be warmed in the oven; bacon and pancake passes must move into the warm oven after cooking; the toast batches must begin when the last pancake pass starts; and the coffee must begin ten minutes after the bacon goes on, with service waiting until the eggs, toast, and coffee are all finished.",
  "servesOrScale": "6 people",
  "deadline": "09:00",
  "constraints": [
    "one electric griddle",
    "one two-slice toaster",
    "one burr grinder",
    "one drip coffee maker",
    "one oven on lowest setting for holding and warming",
    "one cook",
    "all food must be ready to serve by 09:00",
    "pancake batter must rest 20 minutes",
    "six plates must be pre-warmed in the oven",
    "bacon must be moved to the warm oven after cooking",
    "pancakes must be cooked in three passes on the single griddle",
    "each pancake pass must go to the warm oven as it finishes",
    "eggs must be scrambled only after the griddle is lowered to 300°F and settles for 4 minutes",
    "toast must start when the last pancake pass begins",
    "coffee grinding must start ten minutes after the bacon goes on",
    "service must wait for eggs, toast, and coffee to all be ready"
  ]
}
```

A track is one sequential line of work, so steps in that track are ordered and never overlap, while anything happening at the same time belongs on another track. Each step uses exactly one duration kind: `fixed` with `seconds`, `variable` with `minSeconds`, `maxSeconds`, and `defaultSeconds`, or `indefinite` until the person ends it. A step’s start trigger connects it to the clock or another step through `programStart`, `programStartOffset`, `afterStep`, `afterStepWithBuffer`, `manual`, `onAbort`, or `compound`. `stepId`s are unique across the entire program, not just within one track. Every `task` a step occupies needs a matching `resourceConstraints` entry, and `maxConcurrent` is what prevents two steps from sharing one physical resource such as an oven, toaster, or coffee maker. Repeated work should be expressed as `replicates` on one step, with `instances: "each"` for per-repetition follow-on work, `instances: "all"` for the barrier step, and `maxInFlight` when only some repetitions can be in progress because a holding area is full.

Expected resource constraints for this breakfast:

- `griddle` — `maxConcurrent: 1` — one cook; only one electric griddle exists, so all griddle work must be serialized.
- `toaster` — `maxConcurrent: 1` — one cook; one two-slice toaster runs one batch at a time, with the slice capacity handled inside the batch/repetition model rather than by giving multiple toasters.
- `oven` — `maxConcurrent: 1` — one cook; one oven at its lowest setting, used for warm-holding and plate warming.
- `coffee_maker` — `maxConcurrent: 1` — one cook; only one drip coffee maker exists for the brew step.
- `grinder` — `maxConcurrent: 1` — one cook; only one burr grinder exists for the grinding step.
- `cook` — `maxConcurrent: 1` — one person; the only human worker, so active human tasks must not overlap.

```json
{
  "acknowledgement": "tracks are sequential lines of work; one duration kind per step; triggers link steps; every task needs a resourceConstraint; stepIds are global; repeated work uses replicates, instances, and maxInFlight.",
  "resourceConstraints": [
    { "task": "griddle", "maxConcurrent": 1 },
    { "task": "toaster", "maxConcurrent": 1 },
    { "task": "oven", "maxConcurrent": 1 },
    { "task": "coffee_maker", "maxConcurrent": 1 },
    { "task": "grinder", "maxConcurrent": 1 },
    { "task": "cook", "maxConcurrent": 1 }
  ],
  "actors": 1
}
```

Turn 3 of 4 — extraction. Steps only: no tracks, no triggers, no program JSON.

Imagine you have to carry out this recipe yourself, in a kitchen where you have: one griddle, one two-slice toaster, one coffee maker, one oven on its lowest setting, one cook, and everything must be ready at 09:00. You have only the text below. Read all of it.

List every timed activity you would have to perform, in the order the text gives it, with:

- a short kebab-case `stepId` and a human `name`;
- `task`: the resource it occupies while it runs — the oven, a burner, the thermocycler, the PA, the bench, your own hands. Use the same name every time for the same resource;
- how long it takes: exact (`fixed`), a range (`variable`), or "until I decide" (`indefinite`);
- `sourceSpan`: the exact words in the text you took it from, as `{"quote": "...", "occurrence": n}`, where n says which occurrence of those words you mean (1 for the first). Quote the text verbatim — do not paraphrase it;
- `inferred`: `true` for a step the text never states but the work needs anyway (preheating, thawing, resting, cooling, labelling, sound-check), with `"sourceSpan": null`. Keep these few and obvious.

Split anything the text bundles into one sentence when the parts occupy different resources or different stretches of time ("brown the meat, then simmer for 40 minutes" is two activities). Do not decide yet which activities can overlap, which track they belong to, or what waits for what.

Reply with the step list as JSON in a single ```json fenced block:

```json
{
  "steps": [
    {
      "stepId": "roast-turkey",
      "name": "Roast the turkey",
      "task": "oven",
      "duration": { "type": "fixed", "seconds": 10800 },
      "sourceSpan": { "quote": "Roast the turkey for 3 hours", "occurrence": 1 },
      "inferred": false
    },
    {
      "stepId": "rest-turkey",
      "name": "Rest the turkey",
      "task": "counter",
      "duration": { "type": "variable", "minSeconds": 1200, "maxSeconds": 2400, "defaultSeconds": 1800 },
      "sourceSpan": { "quote": "let it rest", "occurrence": 1 },
      "inferred": false
    },
    {
      "stepId": "preheat-oven",
      "name": "Preheat the oven",
      "task": "oven",
      "duration": { "type": "fixed", "seconds": 900 },
      "sourceSpan": null,
      "inferred": true
    }
  ]
}
```

Turn 4 of 4 — relationships, then the program.

Take the step list from turn 3 exactly as it stands.

**First, tracks.** Put each step in a track: one track per parallel line of work — per dish, per station, per instrument, per performer, per sample group. Steps in one track run one after another and must not overlap; anything that runs while something else runs belongs in its own track.

**Second, triggers.** Give every step a `startTrigger` from this vocabulary and no other:

- `{"type":"programStart"}` — at t = 0.
- `{"type":"programStartOffset","offsetSeconds":n}` — n seconds after the start; this is how a short track is delayed so it finishes with the others.
- `{"type":"afterStep","stepId":"x"}` — when x ends. Add `"offsetSeconds"` for a gap, `"event":"start"` to hang off x's start instead of its end, `"instances"` when x is replicated.
- `{"type":"afterStepWithBuffer","stepId":"x","bufferSeconds":n}` — n seconds after x ends.
- `{"type":"manual"}` — the person taps to start it: a gate that no clock can predict (guests seated, dough looks right, the surgeon is ready).
- `{"type":"compound","logic":"all"|"any","triggers":[...]}` — wait for all of, or the first of, several triggers.

**Third, refine the question before you answer it.** Within the scope of scheduling these activities for one person to follow, suggest a better version of the question "which activities depend on which, and which can run at the same time?" — one that would expose dependencies this text implies but does not state: things that must cool, rest, preheat, thaw, proof, be held warm, or be ready at the same moment as something else. Write your improved question out, answer it, and revise the triggers accordingly. A step the improved question reveals is added here, marked `"inferred": true`.

**Then emit the complete program JSON** in a single ```json fenced block: `schemaVersion`, `programId`, `name`, `environmentType`, `actors`, `tracks`, and a `resourceConstraints` entry for every `task` any step uses. Carry turn 3's provenance onto each step as `"metadata": {"sourceSpan": ..., "inferred": ...}`.

```json
{
  "schemaVersion": "0.3.0-alpha",
  "programId": "kebab-case-id",
  "name": "Human title",
  "environmentType": "kitchen",
  "actors": 2,
  "tracks": [
    {
      "trackId": "turkey",
      "name": "Turkey",
      "steps": [
        {
          "stepId": "preheat-oven",
          "name": "Preheat the oven",
          "task": "oven",
          "duration": { "type": "fixed", "seconds": 900 },
          "startTrigger": { "type": "programStart" },
          "metadata": { "sourceSpan": null, "inferred": true }
        },
        {
          "stepId": "roast-turkey",
          "name": "Roast the turkey",
          "task": "oven",
          "duration": { "type": "fixed", "seconds": 10800 },
          "startTrigger": { "type": "afterStep", "stepId": "preheat-oven" },
          "metadata": { "sourceSpan": { "quote": "Roast the turkey for 3 hours", "occurrence": 1 }, "inferred": false }
        }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "resourceConstraints": [
    { "task": "oven", "maxConcurrent": 1 },
    { "task": "counter", "maxConcurrent": 2 }
  ],
  "metadata": { "serves": "8" }
}
```

Then finish the job with the tools:
1. If the public catalog already covers this (search_public_recipes or cook_recipe), load that instead and stop — its result already has the live URL.
2. Otherwise keep the program you just built; `rhylthyme://guide/authoring` is the cheat-sheet and `rhylthyme://examples/*` are complete programs to pattern-match.
3. Express the limits as constraints, not as copied JSON: the `resourceConstraints`, `replicates`, `instances` and `maxInFlight` you confirmed in turn 2.
4. Run validate_program and fix every error it reports.
5. Run analyze_schedule with finishAt="09:00" to check the makespan, critical path and resource conflicts; adjust offsets so tracks finish together. Its `bindingConstraints` say which limit is actually gating the makespan.
6. Call visualize_schedule and give the user the live URL plus the Gantt/itinerary from the result. Do not describe the schedule in prose.
